questions.question: What is the main purpose of GAAP principles?
options: To make bookkeeping faster
To make financial statements trustworthy and comparable between businesses
To reduce the tax a business pays
To replace source documents

questions.question: How do exam questions usually test GAAP principles?
options: By asking you to list all six principles from memory
By giving a scenario and asking which principle is being applied and why
By asking for the year each principle was invented
By testing journal entries only

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the six Grade 10 GAAP principles?
options: Prudence
Going concern
Double taxation
Materiality

questions.question: Land bought for R500 000 in 2019 is now worth R900 000 but is still shown at R500 000. Which principle applies?
options: Prudence
Going concern
Historical cost
Matching

questions.question: Why does accounting prefer the original purchase price over today's estimated value?
options: The purchase price is a verifiable fact supported by a source document; today's value is a changing opinion
Original prices are always lower, which saves tax
Estimated values are illegal to record
It saves time recalculating values every year

questions.question: Which action is an example of PRUDENCE?
options: Recording land at its purchase price
Writing off a doubtful debt instead of keeping it as an asset
Recording a stapler as an expense
Keeping the owner's home out of the business books

questions.question: What is the key difference between historical cost and prudence?
options: There is no difference; they are the same principle
Historical cost applies to liabilities, prudence to assets
Historical cost sticks to the original purchase price; prudence chooses the cautious figure when uncertainty exists
Prudence only applies at year end

subtopics.title: Materiality and the Business Entity Rule

questions.question: A R45 stapler that will last years is recorded as Stationery expense rather than a fixed asset. Which principle justifies this?
options: Materiality
Historical cost
Going concern
Business entity rule

questions.question: When is information considered 'material'?
options: When it is about physical materials like stock
When leaving it out or misstating it would change a reader's decision
When it is more than exactly R1 000
When the owner says it is important

questions.question: The owner pays their home electricity bill from the business bank account. According to the business entity rule this is recorded as:
options: Electricity expense of the business
A liability owed to the municipality
Drawings — a reduction of owner's equity
Nothing — personal payments are ignored completely

questions.question: Which phrase in a scenario is the strongest signal of the business entity rule?
options: 'is now worth more than it cost'
'the owner took cash for personal use'
'too small an amount to matter'
'will continue trading next year'

subtopics.title: Going Concern, Matching, and the Matching Game

questions.question: Financial statements are prepared assuming the business will keep operating into the foreseeable future. This is the principle of:
options: Matching
Going concern
Prudence
Materiality

questions.question: Insurance of R12 000 is paid in March for 12 months, but the financial year ends in June. Matching requires that:
options: The full R12 000 is this year's expense because it was paid this year
Only the portion covering this financial year is expensed; the rest is prepaid
The whole amount is recorded as a liability
The insurance is ignored until next year

questions.question: Wages for the last week of June are only paid in July. Which treatment follows the matching principle?
options: Record them as June's expense, accrued at year end
Record them as July's expense because that is when cash moved
Split them equally between the two years
Record them as Drawings

questions.question: Which question best identifies the principle in any scenario?
options: 'How big is the business?'
'What is the accountant refusing to do, or insisting on doing?'
'Which journal was used?'
'Who is the auditor?'
